\begin{CRchronicle}{112}
Three days ran out the year under the Vail roof, and the boy kept a count no roof could read. Stone twenty-eight, twenty-nine and thirty came without a boundary drawn. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order: barley crust two inches from the ear; the empty place holding the fold; the thread frozen and unwiped, for nobody was ever told about the thread; cold stopping at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody would perform. He knew a face composed by cold is not composure, and that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed slowly from outside, never rubbed. Under the wool the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped, a hand on the pot handle. Both true, the second louder, neither winning.

On the twenty-eighth the fold was found where put, a finding and not a placing. Sella Vail went to the hearth before the basket, told the coals it was the thaw and set the pot rim two inches beyond his reach. Tarn kept six at the kindling and the seventh at the lip, told the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, and brought his ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped. Jorra Vail parted dusty from clean forearms as clot from vessel and put his bent finger into the cold damper. Answers 349 and 350; the count stood at 387.

On the twenty-ninth the day went thin through the finger’s-width door. Ilva at the well answered the woman who asked what Stone’s firings had taken: \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} — her hand to the sleeve before her eyes to the asker, the notched strip unread in the fold. The loan stayed uncalled and Jorra’s promise was neither given nor withdrawn. Answers 351 and 352; the count stood at 388.

On the thirtieth the year’s third and last Account-day and market came before first light. Sella set the basket in the moot-post’s shade. Berr Clay wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} and sent the figure twice over the basket; he called the levy and denied it with \emph{your house}, never I, and went off up the road with the box locked and Stone’s last true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. Twelve arithmetics stood behind one unsigned figure: twelve were twelve and not one account, the figure read not the figure paid, no signature, no doctrine out of twelve. Hessa carried the narrow slate unread; the bell went four, four and a gap. Answers 353 and 354; the count stood at 389 exact, six months and two hundred and nine days told by nobody. Nothing under the roof stood up and called itself an account. The surgeon’s satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found cost nothing, which was how he knew it was not peace.
\end{CRchronicle}
